# Python Package Structure Generated by DotWrap

This directory contains the Python package structure generated by DotWrap for .NET libraries. The structure is designed to map C# namespaces directly to Python submodules, making it intuitive for Python developers to consume .NET libraries.

## Namespace-Based Submodules

C# namespaces are mapped to Python submodules. For example, given the following C# code:

```csharp
namespace MyLib.Data.Models
{
    [DotWrapExpose]
    public class User { }
}

namespace MyLib.Services
{
    [DotWrapExpose]
    public class UserService { }
}
```

The generated Python package would look like:

```
python_project_root/
├── setup.py
└── my_project
    ├── __init__.py # must contain the line "from .__dotwrap_generated.__dotwrap_exports import *"
    ├── ... user can add their own stuff here
    └── _dotwrap_generated/
        ├── __init__.py
        ├── __dotwrap_exports.py # export visible types and top-level modules
        |   # Creating modules with special names (e.g. collections) in the lower level was causing issues for me
        ├── modules/
        |   ├── __init__.py
        |   ├── data.py
        |   ├── models.py
        |   └── services.py
        ├── main.py
        └── lib_build.py
```

-   Each C# namespace becomes a Python submodule.
-   The `__dotwrap_generated` folder contains the generated wrapper code for each namespace.
-   The `main.py` file inside `__dotwrap_generated` contains the Python classes that wrap the corresponding C# classes.
-   `__init__.py` files are included to ensure proper module initialization and import behavior.

## Notes

-   The structure supports deep namespace hierarchies and multiple exposed classes.
-   All generated code is placed under `_dotwrap_generated` to separate it from user-authored Python code.
-   This approach enables clean, maintainable, and discoverable Python packages for .NET libraries.

For more details, see the main project documentation or the [DotWrap GitHub repository](https://github.com/connorivy/DotWrap).
